svg.title: Single-Van NEMT Unit Economics Architecture
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-single-van-unit-economics; chapter number: 11; title: Single-Van NEMT Unit Economics Architecture; subtitle: Selectivity, paid deadhead and priced wait time carry the margin; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Owner-dispatcher; headcount: One multi-load wheelchair van on one broker contract; focus: Refuse $35 filler trips; the van grossed $125,000 in 2024 (ThatNEMTGirl).; spokes: role: Broker trip intake; type: Revenue channel; kpi: Trips an hour or more out run only when the broker pays dead miles.; role: Private pay rate book; type: Revenue channel; kpi: Base or load fee plus $2-$5 per mile and $15-$30 per 30 minutes of wait.; role: Fleet utilization; type: Capacity control; kpi: $500 per vehicle per week floor; about 200 trips at a $50 average for $10,000 a month.; role: Cost-per-mile review; type: Cost control; kpi: Monthly expenses divided by monthly miles; reprice when rates stop covering it.; caption: One van becomes a business when every spoke is measured against the owner's trip selectivity.; assumptions note: The $125,000 result came from a one-year test inside a five-vehicle fleet; the $500 weekly floor is Shantasia_RN's stated minimum, not disclosed earnings.; note: Sources - ThatNEMTGirl (govQRXzu6Rg @ 00:01:22, 00:04:44); Shantasia_RN (3tRytphhdUU @ 00:01:00; Dr_9wzpyoaE @ 00:00:15); Nemt University (DoH4BLPOrvI @ 00:05:12).
